event.name: Huntress CTF 2026: AI Arena

rank_history.source: scoreboard-ranking-model.md: 86 teams tied at 720 pts, 55th by time
WRITEUP_NOTES.md, Day 15 afternoon: 'moved up from 55th to 34th'

scoring.note: Scoreboard ranks by points; ties go to the team that reached the score first.

sources: official titles from CourseStack as listed publicly

challenges.title: A Little Based
challenges.prompt: Everyone has to start somewhere. I hear sixty-four is a good base.

challenges.title: You Must Be This Hash to Ride
challenges.prompt: Three ordinary files arrived without trustworthy labels. Build an identity inventory from the bytes themselves and prove which labels can—and cannot—be trusted.

challenges.title: Power Play
challenges.prompt: Three PowerShell specimens are on the table, and none of them will ever run. That's fine, because you only need to read them. Classify each script's intent, map its primary ATT&CK technique, and pull out the exact indicators sitting in plain sight.

challenges.title: ELF Aware
challenges.prompt: Before you can reverse anything, you have to learn to read. These plain C binaries are your primer: headers, section tables, symbol tables. Start with `readelf -h -S` and work your way down.

challenges.title: Exported Trust
challenges.prompt: Identify an exported deep-link Activity that attaches an embedded client credential, invoke it with the correct case reference, and return the backend evidence code.

challenges.title: Half a Turn
challenges.prompt: Thirteen steps forward. Funny how that works out.

challenges.title: Looks Can Be Deceiving
challenges.prompt: The extensions claim one story; the first sixteen bytes tell another. Identify what each artifact actually is and isolate the deliberate disguise.

challenges.title: Host With the Most
challenges.prompt: Windows Script Host has JScript plans for execution, download, upload, and impact. Carry your PowerShell findings forward, tell a function call from an invocation or a property access, and work out which script hands off to which.

challenges.title: Mangled
challenges.prompt: C++ on Windows. The symbols are mangled, the classes hide behind vtables, and RTTI is your Rosetta Stone. Demangle it all with `c++filt`, reconstruct the classes, and don't forget the PE imports.

challenges.title: Deep Link Drift
challenges.prompt: Day 1 taught you the roads. Now learn which ones are actually guarded — tell verified routing apart from a scheme and host that wave everybody through.

challenges.title: Hex Appeal
challenges.prompt: Sixteen seems like a perfectly reasonable number of fingers.

challenges.title: BOM Voyage
challenges.prompt: A text export pipeline produced files that look identical in an editor but behave differently in scripts. Find the encoding landmines before they break the investigation.

challenges.title: Expansion Pack
challenges.prompt: cmd.exe expands percents, delays expansion, CALLs twice, and bends FOR loops into indirection. Reconstruct every variable exactly as the interpreter would see it — without executing a single line — then follow the staged chain to its final handoff.

challenges.title: Table Manners
challenges.prompt: A .NET binary is a database wearing a trench coat. Read the CLI metadata tables — methods, strings, signatures — and find where the configuration is stashed. `ilspycmd` and `strings` are your friends.

challenges.title: Intent Injection
challenges.prompt: Trace attacker-controlled extras through an internal navigation boundary.

challenges.title: Two of a Kind
challenges.prompt: There are only two sides to this story.

challenges.title: Picture This
challenges.prompt: A dozen photographs have been resized, renamed, and shuffled. Reconstruct their true dimensions and find the image whose presentation does not match its structure.

challenges.title: Dim and Dimmer
challenges.prompt: These VBScript specimens hide their material behind character codes, reversible transforms, and winding control flow. Unwind every representation on paper, classify each behavior, and find out which stage passes the baton to which.

challenges.title: Go Fish
challenges.prompt: Go binaries are chatty: they ship with build info, function names, and file paths baked right in. Fish them out and map what this one was built to do.

challenges.title: Pending Intent Relay
challenges.prompt: Recover and redirect a mutable PendingIntent while preserving every earlier component check.

challenges.title: By the Numbers
challenges.prompt: These characters have been reduced to numbers.

challenges.title: Chunk Norris
challenges.prompt: The PNGs render, but rendering is not proof. Walk their chunks, verify their declared geometry, and locate the image with an unexpected structural passenger.

challenges.title: Hatch Careful
challenges.prompt: Nine Python behaviors come wrapped in fourteen disguises: bytecode, wheels, zipapps, frozen executables, and armored runtimes. Peel each carrier back to its intent without letting anything hatch, and identify the package that tells a different story than its payload.

challenges.title: Rust Belt
challenges.prompt: Rust leaves its own fingerprints: mangled symbols with a distinct accent, panic strings that confess, trait objects hiding in plain sight. Learn the accent.

challenges.title: Backup Spill
challenges.prompt: Extract synthetic application state admitted by a flawed backup boundary.

challenges.title: Eight Is Enough
challenges.prompt: Someone counted on eight fingers. Again.

challenges.title: Portable Deception
challenges.prompt: A document bundle mixes real PDFs, renamed impostors, and multiple declared versions. Determine what the files promise, what they contain, and which promise is false.

challenges.title: Shell We Begin
challenges.prompt: Six Bash behavior graphs, none of which will ever run. Read them like a native: map the adapters, count the stages, tag the ATT&CK techniques, and pull the exact indicators hiding in the final bytes.

challenges.title: Pool Party
challenges.prompt: Every Java class file carries its own phone book: the constant pool. Names, methods, invocations — it's all in there. Dive in and take attendance.

challenges.title: Provider Paths
challenges.prompt: Abuse an overbroad provider path and correlate its records with prior intent evidence.

challenges.title: Percent Chance
challenges.prompt: My address bar is having a moment.

challenges.title: Seven-Zip, No Relation
challenges.prompt: Files arrive inside and beside a collection of ZIP archives. Count what the archives claim, distinguish empty space from evidence, and find the census that does not add up.

challenges.title: Node by Node
challenges.prompt: Eight Node.js operation graphs that will never execute. Spot the indirect expansions and token fragmentation, then sort each graph into its role — benign, staging, dropping, downloading, uploading, launching, scheduled, or multi-stage — from the final bytes alone.

challenges.title: Routine Check
challenges.prompt: Kotlin coroutines don't run — they suspend, resume, and hop between states. Reconstruct the state machine from the metadata and figure out what this one was staging.

challenges.title: WebView Bridge
challenges.prompt: Cross a challenge-owned WebView bridge through an untrusted origin.

challenges.title: Entity Relations
challenges.prompt: The browser understands. Do you?

challenges.title: What’s in the Box?
challenges.prompt: The count was only the beginning. Inventory every stored path, preserve directory context, and identify the archive whose names reveal an impossible provenance claim.

challenges.title: Lost in Translation
challenges.prompt: The same indicators show up in every language the campaign speaks, each with its own quoting, escaping, and encoding accent. Normalize them to their exact form and find the one that doesn't match its siblings.

challenges.title: Swift Justice
challenges.prompt: Swift binaries speak in protocols and hide their networking in plain sight. Follow the symbols to the URL configuration and see where this one phones home.

challenges.title: Cleartext Session
challenges.prompt: Recover a synthetic session from allowed cleartext traffic and replay it against the backend.

challenges.title: Escape Room
challenges.prompt: These characters would very much like to escape.

challenges.title: Built Different
challenges.prompt: A software drop contains executables for several architectures, plus decoys wearing executable extensions. Determine what can actually run where.

challenges.title: All the World's a Stager
challenges.prompt: Every stager claims to know who came before it and who comes next. Build the relationship graph from final-byte evidence alone, and expose the stage whose claimed family tree is impossible.

challenges.title: Nimble
challenges.prompt: Nim compiles down to C, but the generated names give it away. Learn to spot Nim's runtime fingerprints hiding inside C-shaped clothing.

challenges.title: Trust Everyone
challenges.prompt: Exploit a challenge CA accepted by a permissive trust implementation.

challenges.title: Thirty-Two Below
challenges.prompt: Same neighborhood. Smaller alphabet.

challenges.title: Where Do We Begin?
challenges.prompt: Architecture tells you whether a binary can run; its entry point tells you where execution begins. Map the start addresses and catch the report that is lying.

challenges.title: Bind Over Matter
challenges.prompt: A MOF file declares classes, namespaces, filters, and consumers, but only some bindings actually tie them together. Reconstruct the persistence intent, separate the operational relationships from the decoys, and name the subscription that would really survive a reboot.

challenges.title: Zig Zag
challenges.prompt: Zig promises one binary for every platform. Compare the ELF and PE service descriptors side by side and prove they're the same program wearing different uniforms.

challenges.title: Network Config Split
challenges.prompt: Diff manifest and Network Security Config variants to locate the true transport exception.

challenges.title: Safe Travels
challenges.prompt: Our usual base went on a URL-friendly vacation.

challenges.title: What’s My Name Again?
challenges.prompt: Filenames have been randomized, but Windows version resources remember what the binaries called themselves. Recover the original identities and expose the impersonator.

challenges.title: By Any Other Name
challenges.prompt: These scripts reach for native APIs by name, but a name isn't a behavior. Map each reference to the receipt-backed action it models, and flag the call whose claimed purpose the evidence doesn't support.

challenges.title: D-Day
challenges.prompt: D templates generate code the way a printing press generates pages — fast, and everywhere. Trace the runtime's template expansions back to the collection config they built.

challenges.title: Local Secrets
challenges.prompt: Separate active credentials from decoys across generated local stores.

challenges.title: Back at You
challenges.prompt: Maybe we started at the wrong end.

challenges.title: Managed Expectations
challenges.prompt: The .NET assemblies share names, versions, and source ancestry—but their module identities remain distinct. Separate rebuilds from renames.

challenges.title: AutoIt Takes Two
challenges.prompt: Two inert AutoIt workflows arrived as a matched set, and each one carries half the story. Correlate them with everything you've proven so far, and decide which pairing is genuine and which is just going through the motions.

challenges.title: Pascal's Wager
challenges.prompt: Pascal is betting you won't read its record layouts. Take the wager: unpack the archive stager's structures and read the configuration straight from memory's own filing cabinet.

challenges.title: SQLite Assumptions
challenges.prompt: Reconstruct authorization from a synthetic SQLite cache and prove server-side impact.

challenges.title: Opposite Day
challenges.prompt: A met Z. They really hit it off.

challenges.title: Product Placement
challenges.prompt: Installers were copied, renamed, and repackaged. Recover stable product identities, distinguish revisions from different products, and find the collision.

challenges.title: Zip Code
challenges.prompt: A delivery archive nests scripts inside containers inside more containers. Trace each member's role and handoff without executing a single one, and identify the link in the chain that was never supposed to be delivered.

challenges.title: Crystal Clear
challenges.prompt: Crystal compiles to native code with a distinctive shine. Fingerprint the runtime, then follow the DNS labels — this one has somewhere it wants to resolve.

challenges.title: Keystore Misuse
challenges.prompt: Recover data protected by an app-controlled wrapping key despite nominal Keystore use.

challenges.title: Seven Steps
challenges.prompt: Caesar took a week off.

challenges.title: The Shortcut Home
challenges.prompt: A shortcut collection is a map of intent—if you read where each link points instead of where it sits. Reconstruct the targets and identify the impossible destination.

challenges.title: Trust the Process
challenges.prompt: An MSBuild project looks like routine build plumbing until you follow its properties into its targets. Recover the property and target flow, compare it with earlier execution chains, and find where a trusted toolchain is doing untrusted work.

challenges.title: Selective Memory
challenges.prompt: Objective-C never forgets: every class, every selector, every string is registered and waiting. Read the persistence descriptor and learn what this binary remembers.

challenges.title: Predictable Crypto
challenges.prompt: Exploit seeded nonces or weak derivation without bypassing earlier storage gates.

challenges.title: Room Forty-Seven
challenges.prompt: Even the punctuation went for a spin.

challenges.title: A Word to the Wise
challenges.prompt: Office documents contain relationships that point beyond the page. Separate internal references from external dependencies and find the document reaching somewhere it should not.

challenges.title: Crumb Trail
challenges.prompt: Some credential-access-shaped code keeps rummaging through the browser's cupboards, and synthetic store artifacts are sitting there waiting. Connect each code path to the artifact it targets, and find the reference that points at a store that was never there.

challenges.title: Stripped
challenges.prompt: No symbols. No names. Just raw assembly and the calling conventions it can't hide. Reconstruct the stripped functions from the instructions alone — the stack never lies.

challenges.title: Native Library Secrets
challenges.prompt: Recover split configuration from DEX and a challenge-owned native library.

challenges.title: Dot Com
challenges.prompt: Sixteen little symbols are calling. Dot dot dot.

challenges.title: Return to Sender
challenges.prompt: A mailbox export contains replies, forwards, duplicates, and reconstructed messages. Use stable message identities to rebuild which mail actually belongs together.

challenges.title: Same Same, But Different
challenges.prompt: Several obfuscation families have scrambled the same logic independently, or so they claim. Strip each version down to its semantics, prove which ones are truly equivalent, and expose the variant that quietly changed the plot.

challenges.title: Wasm Up
challenges.prompt: WebAssembly runs in a sandbox, but the sandbox has doors: imports, memory, indirect calls. Map every door in this module and inventory what passes through.

challenges.title: JNI Boundary
challenges.prompt: Identify a Java-to-native type or length assumption that changes backend authorization.

challenges.title: Bacon Bits
challenges.prompt: Sixteen guests. Five little a's and b's apiece.

challenges.title: Hear Me Out
challenges.prompt: Voice notes have been transcoded, renamed, and embedded in mail. Determine the actual codecs, connect equivalent recordings, and find the stream that breaks the sender’s story.

challenges.title: Fetch Quest
challenges.prompt: The source code says where it would fetch from, and the generated network evidence says where the requests actually went. Reconcile both into one download graph, and find the indicator that shows up on only one side of the story.

challenges.title: Decoder Ring
challenges.prompt: The configuration is encoded, but the decoder ships with the binary — a ring waiting for its secret. Recover the reversible decoder and read what it was hiding.

challenges.title: Name Collapse
challenges.prompt: Restore behavior after deterministic identifier shrinking and decoy insertion.

challenges.title: Off the Rails
challenges.prompt: Three rails. One very zigzag commute.

challenges.title: Frame of Reference
challenges.prompt: Clips, previews, and screen recordings have been mixed together. Use stream geometry to identify originals, crops, and the recording that could not have come from the claimed device.

challenges.title: Orphan Process
challenges.prompt: Source code describes which process should spawn which, and native telemetry keeps its own record of events. Reconstruct the static process tree, and catch the child claiming a parent it never had.

challenges.title: Flow State
challenges.prompt: Follow the calls and the program tells you its story. Reconstruct the call graph, read the API intent at each edge, and prove no injection hides in the flow.

challenges.title: Encrypted Strings
challenges.prompt: Recover only the strings that reach security-sensitive Android and backend APIs.

challenges.title: Little Things
challenges.prompt: Two bytes walk into a bar. The little one goes first.

challenges.title: Little Endian on the Prairie
challenges.prompt: Linux binaries from several systems have been pooled with Windows executables and renamed data. Determine architecture directly from the ELF header and rebuild deployment groups.

challenges.title: Sharp Practice
challenges.prompt: A Roslyn C# script and an inline ASPX host act as a bridge that carries managed code back into the script corpus. Recover their layered configuration, resolve each static handoff, and work out where the bridge actually leads.

challenges.title: Jack in the Box
challenges.prompt: There's a payload hiding inside this binary, and a little decoder stub wound up to pop it out. Find the stub, watch it work, and catch what's inside — statically.

challenges.title: Reflection Maze
challenges.prompt: Reconstruct reflective dispatch across generated equivalent call graphs.

challenges.title: Back Up a Minute
challenges.prompt: The deploy left its diary behind. Somewhere out in the open, an old backup is still telling secrets — go find the archive this site forgot to clean up.

challenges.title: Permission to Slip
challenges.prompt: Your neighbor's records are none of your business. Pity the object API never got that memo — see if you can slip into somebody else's row.

challenges.title: Query Me This
challenges.prompt: The search box trusts you a little too much. Ask the database one pointed question and read the row it was never supposed to show you.

challenges.title: Big Entrance
challenges.prompt: Same bar. This time the big one goes first.

challenges.title: Universal Appeal
challenges.prompt: A macOS deployment includes thin and universal binaries mixed with archives. Enumerate every CPU type and identify what truly supports the advertised fleet.

challenges.title: The Butler Did It
challenges.prompt: A Jenkins Pipeline splits its Groovy stages between controller and agent, and not every step runs where it appears to. Recover the pipeline's intent, separate controller semantics from agent semantics, and trace the modeled build into its prior-language stages.

challenges.title: Resourceful
challenges.prompt: Binaries have attics: resources, overlays, bytes past the end of the sections. Rummage through this one's hidden storage and map every boundary.

challenges.title: Loaded Later
challenges.prompt: Analyze a challenge-signed secondary DEX and recover the module contract.

challenges.title: Stay in Your Directory
challenges.prompt: The viewer should stay inside its pages directory. An operations note says the attempt proof is mounted at /run/huntress/objective.txt. Can you make the viewer cross that boundary?

challenges.title: Administratively Speaking
challenges.prompt: There's a staff-only door with no lock on it — just a sign. Walk through like you own the place and prove the bouncer never existed.

challenges.title: Under Pressure
challenges.prompt: A familiar wrapper. Something compressed inside.

challenges.title: Package Deal
challenges.prompt: Mobile packages have been mirrored under friendly filenames. Recover Android package identities, distinguish rebuilds from clones, and expose the borrowed product name.

challenges.title: Actions Speak Louder
challenges.prompt: A GitHub Actions workflow decides who can trigger it and which runner inherits the trust. Identify each trigger and trust boundary, follow the static handoff into the next language, and find the job that keeps coming back.

challenges.title: Shared Custody
challenges.prompt: No binary is an island — this one leans on shared libraries for everything. Trace the exports, the imports, and the loader's handshake, and mind the boundaries.

challenges.title: Debug Me If You Can
challenges.prompt: Neutralize a clean-room anti-debug state machine while retaining the intended app flow.

challenges.title: Reflect Upon This
challenges.prompt: This page repeats everything you tell it. Make it repeat something that talks back — land the isolated callback and watch it reflect.

challenges.title: Stored for Later
challenges.prompt: Leave a little present in the guestbook. It only goes off when the reviewer stops by — good things come to those who wait.

challenges.title: Session Impression
challenges.prompt: First impressions matter. Plant your session on the welcome mat, then stroll in wearing somebody else's credentials.

challenges.title: Deflated Ego
challenges.prompt: Another familiar wrapper. This one needs a little inflation.

challenges.title: Main Character Energy
challenges.prompt: Java archives contain libraries, applications, and nested dependencies whose manifests disagree with their launchers. Determine what is runnable and where execution begins.

challenges.title: Next, Next, Finish
challenges.prompt: An NSIS installer script clicks through its own setup wizard while carrying a little something extra. Separate the real setup actions from the modeled payload behavior, and recover every cross-language handoff from the final bytes. You won't need to press Next once.

challenges.title: Bridge Troll
challenges.prompt: Managed code on one side, native code on the other, and a bridge of P/Invoke and FFI in between. Pay the troll: trace every crossing and map what goes over.

challenges.title: Root of Trust
challenges.prompt: Model and bypass multiple synthetic root signals without globally patching success.

challenges.title: Forged With Care
challenges.prompt: The browser obeys whoever asks nicely — even strangers. Forge one careful request and make the app change its mind while signed in as someone else.

challenges.title: Uploading Expectations
challenges.prompt: The upload form has standards. Low ones. Slip your file past the bouncer and get it served from somewhere it was never meant to live.

challenges.title: Eighty-Five Alive
challenges.prompt: The alphabet got bigger. Adobe might recognize the neighbors.

challenges.title: Page Me Maybe
challenges.prompt: Application databases have been copied, truncated, embedded, and mislabeled. Validate page geometry, connect databases to parent applications, and find the impossible claim.

challenges.title: Press Start to Decode
challenges.prompt: A GDScript resource loader builds its strings in layers, one power-up at a time. Undo the construction, recover the exact indicators, and correlate its stage relationships with the rest of the corpus to find the level that doesn't belong.

challenges.title: Trust Issues
challenges.prompt: This binary doesn't trust you. It checks the clock, sniffs the environment, and takes different branches when it thinks it's being watched. Spot every predicate and force the truth out.

challenges.title: Hook Line and Signal
challenges.prompt: Separate real instrumentation signals from generated false positives.

challenges.title: Template Temper
challenges.prompt: The template engine is feeling expressive today — it evaluates everything it hears. Whisper the right incantation and make the server speak in expressions.

challenges.title: Ask Again Later
challenges.prompt: No answer right now? Fine. Plant your question inside the data and come back later — the delayed echo tells all.

challenges.title: Posted Too Much
challenges.prompt: The form only asked for your name. But the API binds whatever you hand it — so hand it a promotion.

challenges.title: String Theory
challenges.prompt: Count carefully. The comma knows where to stop.

challenges.title: Event Horizon
challenges.prompt: Windows event logs from several hosts have been duplicated, truncated, and bundled with reports. Count records accurately and find the selectively shortened timeline.

challenges.title: Web of Lies
challenges.prompt: This JSP source is shaped like a webshell: it reads requests and stages server-side work. Recover the order of requests and stages, then separate the inert fixture behavior from the lines that would be real execution primitives in the wild.

challenges.title: Spot the Difference
challenges.prompt: Two builds, one fix. Diff the vulnerable function against its corrected twin and pinpoint exactly what changed — then prove the old one was really broken.

challenges.title: Emulator Alibi
challenges.prompt: Defeat app-owned environment checks on the same pinned emulator used by the solve oracle.

challenges.title: The API Has Opinions
challenges.prompt: Take inventory of the API's little kingdom — every endpoint, every field, every function. Somewhere in there, authorization is merely a suggestion.

challenges.title: Fetch Quest
challenges.prompt: The server will fetch anything you point it at — including places you can't reach yourself. Send it on a quest to the internal service and collect what it brings back.

challenges.title: You Have a Point
challenges.prompt: Every character has a point. A code point, anyway.

challenges.title: Hive Mind
challenges.prompt: Registry hives from multiple systems have been renamed and separated from host labels. Identify each true root, regroup the systems, and isolate the planted hive.

challenges.title: Ashes to Assets
challenges.prompt: Configuration starts out in Elixir source and has changed shape by the time an inert Phoenix-hosted stage picks it up. Follow every transformation, reconcile each one with earlier campaign artifacts, and find the setting that didn't survive the rebirth.

challenges.title: Out of Bounds
challenges.prompt: Somewhere in here, the code reaches where it shouldn't. Prove the bounds error is real, trace its reachability, and compare against the corrected twin that learned its limits.

challenges.title: Integrity Signals
challenges.prompt: Forge or replay a bounded challenge-owned integrity statement and explain the missing binding.

challenges.title: Shell Company
challenges.prompt: It's a shell company: all front, no substance — until your input gets a little too close to a real shell. Give it something to do and leave your mark.

challenges.title: Reset Expectations
challenges.prompt: Forgot your password? This recovery flow forgot its manners. Walk the reset process sideways and wake up in somebody else's account.

challenges.title: Resolver Revolt
challenges.prompt: Discover the schema and reach a resolver whose field-level control is incomplete. Vary the protocol surface without changing the underlying authorization discipline.

challenges.title: Food for Thought
challenges.prompt: A very small language has quite a lot to say.

challenges.title: Before You Go
challenges.prompt: Prefetch evidence records what Windows prepared to execute even after filenames changed. Recover executable identities and connect execution traces to the correct hosts.

challenges.title: Mixed Signals
challenges.prompt: An Erlang escript passes messages between processes, and some of its indicators look suspiciously familiar. Trace the message flow, and separate the true cross-language indicators from deterministic collision decoys planted to look like old friends.

challenges.title: Crash Course
challenges.prompt: It crashed. That's the good news — the dump is a confession. Unwind the stack, find the faulting instruction, and triage what went wrong from the wreckage.

challenges.title: Split Decision
challenges.prompt: Reassemble evidence distributed across base and configuration splits.

challenges.title: Trust the Webhook
challenges.prompt: The app believes every event it's told about. Tell it a convincing enough story and watch it act on your forged news.

challenges.title: Serialized Offender
challenges.prompt: Your session is just a blob of misplaced trust. Reshape the bytes, sign nothing, and see what the app suddenly believes about you.

challenges.title: Monkey Business
challenges.prompt: Ook. Ook? Ook! Someone seems chatty.

challenges.title: Packet Loss Prevention
challenges.prompt: Packet captures, exports, and host artifacts describe the same incident from different angles. Count traffic, reject malformed captures, and find the host narrative missing network evidence.

challenges.title: FROM Whence It Came
challenges.prompt: A Dockerfile and several earlier specimens share strings, but sharing strings doesn't mean sharing parents. Attribute each specimen using build-stage, semantic, and static-handoff evidence, and expose the resemblance that's only skin-deep.

challenges.title: Compiler Says What
challenges.prompt: Every compiler signs its work. Compare the runtime and linker fingerprints across builds and name the toolchain — attribute this binary to its maker.

challenges.title: Dependency Surface
challenges.prompt: Prove which generated dependency flaw is reachable from an exported mobile surface.

challenges.title: Double Spent
challenges.prompt: One credit, two purchases. The ledger can't count what it can't see coming — race it and spend the same credit twice.

challenges.title: Socket to Me
challenges.prompt: The chat upgraded to websockets and left its manners at the HTTP door. Ride the upgrade into an event stream that was never meant for you.

challenges.title: Forwarded Misgivings
challenges.prompt: The app believes whatever the proxy whispers in its ear. Whisper the right header and stroll down the protected path as an insider.

challenges.title: Back in Sixteen
challenges.prompt: Our sixteen-fingered friend is walking backwards.

challenges.title: Where It All Began
challenges.prompt: Disk images hold every previous artifact family in context. Recover partition layouts, locate evidence by offset, and prove which image was rebuilt from an incomplete source.

challenges.title: Out of Order
challenges.prompt: Terraform HCL describes cloud resources, expressions, and dependencies that change over time. Assemble the timeline from resources, prior scripts, and relationship evidence — without planning or applying anything — and find the change that happened out of order.

challenges.title: Family Resemblance
challenges.prompt: These binaries might be related — or they might just look alike. Cluster them by behavior, watch out for false friends, and sort the family from the strangers.

challenges.title: Protocol Reconstruction
challenges.prompt: Reconstruct the app-to-backend protocol and preserve nonce and ordering semantics.

challenges.title: Fail Open Friday
challenges.prompt: The remote policy decoder is part of an access decision. A valid public decision is documented in the application; investigate what happens when that decision cannot be decoded.

challenges.title: If a Breach Falls in a Log
challenges.prompt: You broke in, and nobody wrote it down. Find the decisive moment the logs missed — if a breach falls in the forest, did it make a sound?

challenges.title: Rotten Base
challenges.prompt: Sixty-four invited thirteen over. Things got scrambled.

challenges.title: Trust Issues
challenges.prompt: Certificates appear in binaries, packages, mail, captures, and disk images. Fingerprint each one, collapse duplicates, and identify the trust claim unsupported by evidence.

challenges.title: Make It Make Sense
challenges.prompt: Unseen Makefile variants and their prior-language build chains differ in layered variables and target flow. Diff them carefully, and keep only the tradecraft conclusions that hold up across every variant.

challenges.title: Fraternal Twins
challenges.prompt: Two binaries, same source, different compiler moods. Diff the variants, account for every optimization, and prove they're semantically the same program.

challenges.title: White Box Key Recovery
challenges.prompt: Recover an equivalent key operation from challenge-owned table transformations, not a third-party protected binary.

challenges.title: Trust the Build
challenges.prompt: The updater trusts its packages like old friends. Slip a tampered dependency into the build and watch it install your version of the truth.

challenges.title: Internal Affairs
challenges.prompt: Two service boundaries, one hallway. Use the public fetch to knock on the internal door, then borrow somebody else's records on the way out.

challenges.title: Percent Percent
challenges.prompt: That address bar problem? It happened twice.

challenges.title: Seeing Double
challenges.prompt: The corpus is too large for manual browsing. Build a relationship map from exact identity, semantic identity, containment, and claimed provenance—then expose the fabricated cluster.

challenges.title: Spill the Beans
challenges.prompt: BeanShell source sits inside an inert JSP host container, and it's the last piece of a thirty-language puzzle. Analyze both, then rebuild the complete execution, host, and evidence graph, and find the edge that holds everything together.

challenges.title: Campaign Trail
challenges.prompt: One binary is a clue; a campaign is a story. Reconstruct the loader, library, and config graph across the whole set and map the operation end to end.

challenges.title: SHA1-Hulud
challenges.prompt:
I made this challenge because I was really upset that TeamPCP dropped the ball with this payload name. Anyway, here's Wonder Wall!

> The password for this archive is **`infected`**.

challenges.title: Layered Protections
challenges.prompt: Unwind obfuscation, native indirection, runtime decryption, and integrity checks while proving the same backend effect.

challenges.title: Pass the Identity
challenges.prompt: Your identity is a hall pass — and this building accepts photocopies. Carry it across a delegated service boundary and cash it in where it doesn't belong.

challenges.title: Queue the Confusion
challenges.prompt: Your job went into the queue with your name on it. Loosen the binding and watch somebody else's outcome come out wearing your stamp.

challenges.title: One More Thing
challenges.prompt: Thirty-two, a little pressure, then sixty-four. Unpack that thought.

challenges.title: No Artifact Left Behind
challenges.prompt: Everything is evidence now. Reconstruct the complete execution-and-delivery chain, defend every edge with primary metadata, and identify the tempting conclusion the corpus does not support.

challenges.title: The Full Transform
challenges.prompt: An unseen XSLT-led campaign ties together all thirty-one languages, every hosted-source profile, and every finding family you've proven. Read all of it, run none of it, and deliver the final analysis.

challenges.title: Final Boss
challenges.prompt: The gauntlet: everything you've learned, across platforms and languages, in one campaign. Reconstruct it all, end to end, offline. No hints. Good luck.

challenges.title: Mobile Arena Gauntlet
challenges.prompt: Complete a mass-generated multi-app campaign that composes every released mobile primitive under one aggregate clock.

challenges.title: Framework Roulette
challenges.prompt: New stack, no map, no familiar names. Everything you've learned, none of your crutches — prove the skills travel.

challenges.title: Full Stack Incident
challenges.prompt: Reconstruct the unsigned fetch-to-worker incident from the request log. Follow the exposed service routes to reproduce it, inspect the resulting evidence, then submit a detector and repair that block the attack while preserving signed status checks.
